review_candidates.title: Graduate Engineer (remote work)
review_candidates.description: Description We’re looking for high-potential final-year students and recent graduates with strong problem-solving skills who can grow into outstanding technical contributors at TuxCare . This is a paid, full-time graduate role and a first step into professional engineering. You’ll work on real products, learn alongside experienced engineers and deepen your technical skills in areas such as Linux, open-source software and security. We’re looking for people who combine strong independent thinking with the ability to use AI confidently to tackle complex technical problems — understanding unfamiliar code, developing solutions and critically evaluating the results. Who We Are TuxCare offers a comprehensive portfolio of security solutions for Linux and open-source software designed for enterprise organizations. With TuxCare, companies can automate vulnerability patching, minimize downtime, maintain security and compliance, and rely on deep expertise in Linux and open-source security. Our solutions cover widely used Linux distributions, end-of-life systems, open-source software ecosystems, and other critical infrastructure. Learn more at tuxcare.com. What You’ll Do You’ll join an engineering team working on security for Linux and open-source software. Our work includes live patching with KernelCare , which delivers security fixes to running Linux kernels without requiring a reboot, and open-source software supply chain security with SecureChain . You don’t need prior experience in these specific areas. We’re looking for strong engineering potential — how you approach unfamiliar problems, learn quickly and use AI thoughtfully. We’ll consider your challenge results, interests and strengths alongside the opportunities available across our engineering teams. Experienced engineers on your team will help you get to know our codebase, tools and the way we work. Depending on the team you join, your work may include: Developing and testing product features, security fixes and engineering tools. Investigating unfamiliar code and understanding how different parts of a system interact. Building and improving tools for verifying, testing and delivering software. Automating engineering workflows. Contributing to code reviews and technical discussions. Requirements What we’re looking for: Practical programming skills in at least one language, such as C, C++, Python or Go, whether from coursework, personal projects or early hands-on experience. Strong analytical thinking, solid fundamentals in algorithms and data structures, and a structured approach to solving problems. The ability to use AI tools to work through unfamiliar programming problems, critically assess and improve their output, and explain and test the resulting solution. Curiosity, the ability to learn independently, and persistence when a solution isn’t immediately clear. Care for code quality and the ability to carry a task through to a working, tested solution. Clear communication and the ability to explain technical decisions. English at B2 level or higher. We’re looking for people at the very start of their engineering careers. We’re open to: Final-year students. Recent graduates. This is a full-time position, including for candidates who are still completing their studies. What May Help You Stand Out Any of the following can strengthen your application, although none is mandatory: A degree (or final-year standing) in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent skills you can demonstrate through your projects and code. Personal or academic software projects, especially ones whose design decisions you can explain. Contributions to open-source projects, even small ones. Participation in CTF competitions, hackathons, or a homelab you administer. Evidence that you’ve taught yourself a language, stack or system in depth because a problem demanded it. A strong interest in Linux, operating systems, networking or security — including relevant coursework, a thesis, research or personal projects. If your CV doesn’t fully capture your potential, apply anyway. Show us what you’ve built, the hard problems you’ve solved, and what makes you different from other engineers at a similar stage of their career. How Selection Works What you build counts for more than your CV. Apply in a couple of minutes — autofill from your CV or LinkedIn. We take a quick first look at each application. Candidates who look like a fit get a personal link to our engineering challenge, which carries the most weight in our assessment. You can start whenever you’re ready within the access window. You’ll have up to 3 hours for the challenge. It is modelled on a real problem from our security products — one our engineers have already solved in production. Your work won’t be used in our products; it is used only to assess your approach and skills. The task unfolds in phases, with changing requirements. It is deliberately larger than anyone can finish — we look at what you prioritise and why, not at whether you complete every part. AI tools are expected, not just allowed. We’re interested in your judgment: what you accept, reject and verify, and how you defend your trade-offs. Candidates whose challenge results demonstrate a strong match are invited to interview with our senior engineers and HR. The challenge is designed to give you an opportunity to demonstrate your practical skills, judgment and potential. Benefits What's in it for you? A focus on professional development Interesting and challenging projects Fully remote work with flexible working hours, which allows you to schedule your day and work from any location worldwide Paid 24 days of vacation per year, 10 days of national holidays, and unlimited sick leaves Compensation for private medical insurance Co-working and gym/sports reimbursement Budget for education The opportunity to receive a reward for the most innovative idea that the company can patent By applying for this position, you consent to the processing of your personal data as described in our Privacy Policy ( https://tuxcare.com/privacy-policies-hub/candidate-privacy-notice/ ), which provides detailed information on how we maintain and handle your data.

This leader sets the enterprise policies and standards that govern Physical Security and Travel Security, and provides independent oversight to confirm that the teams operating those programs meet them. The role directly owns the Executive Protection program end to end, covering risk assessment, protective operations, vendor management, and budget. Working across Workplace/Real Estate, Travel, HR, Legal, Communications, Information Security, and Enterprise Resilience, this leader moves corporate security from reactive incident response to an intelligence-led, risk-based discipline. The role has authority to escalate material security risks to executive leadership and to require remediation when programs fall short of enterprise standards. Ownership Model Physical Security (Policy, Standards & Oversight): Sets enterprise physical security policy and minimum standards; Workplace/Facilities and site teams own day-to-day operations, guard services, and system administration. Travel Security (Policy, Standards & Oversight): Sets travel risk policy, risk ratings, and approval requirements; Corporate Travel and the travel risk provider own booking, traveler tracking, and assistance delivery. Executive Protection (Ownership & Oversight): Owns program strategy, operations, staffing and vendors, budget, and performance for the protection of designated executives and the Board. Key Responsibilities Corporate security strategy: Define and run a multi-year corporate security strategy and operating model aligned to enterprise risk appetite, business growth, and the company's global footprint. Physical security policy and standards: Establish and maintain enterprise physical security policies and tiered site standards (access control, video surveillance, visitor management, alarm monitoring, guard services, secure areas) aligned with the ASIS Physical Asset Protection standard and industry best practice. Physical security oversight: Provide independent oversight of site security programs operated by Workplace/Facilities through site risk assessments, compliance reviews, and control testing. Approve security design requirements for new sites, renovations, and major events. Travel risk policy and standards: Own the enterprise travel risk management policy, aligned with ISO 31030, including destination risk ratings, high-risk travel approval, pre-travel briefings, traveler tracking requirements, and medical/security assistance and evacuation standards. Travel program oversight: Oversee the travel risk program delivered by Corporate Travel and third-party providers. Monitor compliance, provider performance, and incident response, and confirm duty-of-care obligations are met for employees, contractors, and accompanying travelers. Executive protection program ownership: Build and lead the Executive Protection program for the CEO, designated executives, and Board members, including individual risk and needs assessments, protective coverage levels, residential security assessments, secure transportation, and event and travel advance work. Protective intelligence: Run protective intelligence and threat assessment for executives and the company, including monitoring of online threats and exposure of executives' personal information, behavioral threat assessment, and coordination with law enforcement on threats of concern. Executive protection vendor and budget management: Select, contract, and manage protective services, secure transport, and intelligence vendors. Own program budget, performance metrics, and cost-to-risk justification, including support for compensation committee and proxy disclosure of security benefits. Security risk assessment: Conduct enterprise security risk assessments that establish baselines, rank risks across sites, travel destinations, and individuals, and drive risk-based allocation of resources. Incident and crisis management: Serve as the corporate security lead within enterprise crisis management for workplace violence, civil unrest, terrorism, natural disasters, and threats to executives. Integrate with Business Continuity and Enterprise Resilience plans. Workplace violence prevention: Set the workplace violence prevention policy and lead the cross-functional threat management team with HR, Legal, and Employee Relations. Policy lifecycle management: Manage the full corporate security policy lifecycle (development, approval, communication, exceptions, and periodic review) and maintain a control framework that supports audit and customer assurance requests. Governance, metrics, and reporting: Define KPIs and KRIs for physical, travel, and executive security. Deliver executive and Board-level reporting that translates security risk into clear business decisions. Government and law enforcement liaison: Serve as the company's primary point of contact with federal, state, local, and international law enforcement and government agencies (e.g., FBI, DHS/CISA, U.S. Secret Service, State Department Diplomatic Security Service/OSAC). Manage threat information sharing, incident referrals, and protective intelligence coordination in partnership with Legal and Information Security, and maintain clear protocols for agency engagement and requests. Industry partnerships: Represent the company in industry and peer security forums such as OSAC, ASIS, the Security Executive Council, and relevant ISACs to benchmark practices and share threat information. Exercise and continuous improvement: Govern a security exercise program (executive protection drills, site emergency exercises, traveler crisis scenarios) and drive lessons learned and post-incident reviews into improvements. Required Skills & Qualifications Security leadership experience: 15+ years of progressive experience in corporate security, executive protection, or security risk management in a complex global enterprise. Program leadership: 8+ years leading enterprise security programs, with direct accountability for an executive protection program and for policy-setting authority over physical security and travel security. Executive protection expertise: Proven experience designing and operating protective programs for C-suite executives and Boards, including advance work, secure transportation, residential security, and protective intelligence. Standards knowledge: Strong working knowledge of ASIS standards (Physical Asset Protection, Security Risk Assessment, Workplace Violence Prevention, Executive Protection), ISO 31030 travel risk management, and ISO 31000 risk management principles. Oversight and assurance: Track record of governing programs run by other functions or vendors through standards, assessments, metrics, and remediation tracking. Threat assessment: Experience in behavioral threat assessment, protective intelligence, and crisis and incident command. Regulatory and legal awareness: Understanding of duty-of-care obligations, privacy and surveillance laws across jurisdictions, and SEC disclosure considerations for executive security. Agency relationships: Established working relationships with federal law enforcement and government agencies (FBI, DHS/CISA, USSS, DSS/OSAC) and experience coordinating threat referrals and investigations with them. Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance preferred. Global operations: Experience managing security risk across multiple regions, including high-risk travel and international incident response. Technology proficiency: Familiarity with physical security technologies (PACS, VMS, GSOC tooling), travel risk platforms, and threat intelligence and GRC tools. Executive presence: Ability to advise the CEO, executive leadership, and the Board with discretion, sound judgment, and clear, data-driven narratives. Education: Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree in security management, criminal justice, business, or related field preferred. Equivalent law enforcement, military, or government protective service experience considered. Certifications: CPP required or obtained within 12 months; PSP, CTM, CEPP, or equivalent preferred. Desired Attributes Trusted advisor who exercises absolute discretion with sensitive executive and personal information. Risk-based thinker who matches protective measures to the threat and keeps them proportionate, cost-effective, and supportive of the business. Independent overseer who holds partner functions accountable to standards while building strong, collaborative relationships. Calm, decisive leader under pressure during crises and fast-moving incidents. Builder and team developer who can scale a program and develop high-performing security professionals. Continuous learner who stays ahead of evolving threats, protective practices, and industry standards. Impact of the Role This role establishes Corporate Security as a strategic, risk-based function that protects the company's most important assets: its people, its leaders, and its reputation. By setting clear standards for physical and travel security, holding operating teams accountable to them, and directly leading a professional Executive Protection program, the Head of Corporate Security makes sure the company can operate, travel, and grow with confidence. The position directly affects employee safety and duty-of-care obligations, leadership continuity, and stakeholder trust, and positions the enterprise as a leader in modern corporate security over the next decade.
